How to read this map

Warning colours
Every building, road segment and district is coloured by the combination of likelihood and potential impact severity using the Flood Risk Matrix above (Speight et al., 2018, Fig. 1). Green means business as usual. Yellow means be aware. Amber means be prepared, and a multiagency tactical response is possible. Red means take action, with danger to life.
Impact severity rules
Buildings (people and property): Minimal below 0.1 m, Minor 0.1 to 0.3 m, Significant 0.3 to 0.76 m, Severe 0.76 m and deeper.
Roads (transport): Minimal below 0.1 m, Minor 0.1 to 0.3 m, Significant 0.3 to 0.5 m (impassable to most vehicles), Severe 0.5 m and deeper.
Where velocity is available, severity is upgraded by the flood hazard rating HR = d x (v + 0.5) + 0.5. An HR of 1.25 or more gives at least Significant, and 2.0 or more gives Severe (danger to people; EA and HR Wallingford, FD2320 and FD2321).
Likelihood rules
FGS bands from ensemble flood-map exceedance probability. Very Low: below 20 percent. Low: 20 to 40 percent. Medium: 40 to 60 percent. High: above 60 percent. Probabilities below 5 percent are below the reporting threshold (Speight et al., 2018).
District overall risk
District impact class follows Speight et al. (2018) Table 1 thresholds. At least one flooded residential property gives Minor. Any residential property at Significant severity or worse, more than 2 non-residential receptors flooded, or more than 5 m of road at Significant severity gives Significant. More than 100 residential properties at Significant severity or worse gives Severe. The impact class is then combined with the district likelihood through the matrix.
Standard: Speight et al. (2018) J Flood Risk Mgmt 11:S884-S901; SEPA and Met Office FGS user guide (2015); EA and HRW flood hazard rating (FD2320, FD2321); WMO No. 1150 IBF guidelines. Product: IBF routine v1, first version for iteration.
